newsitem.title: SPAIN: Argentaria recovery in '97 results to boost shares.
newsitem.headline: Argentaria recovery in '97 results to boost shares.

text.p: Spain's Corporacion Bancaria de Espana (Argentaria) will see an improvement in its 1997 results giving its shares a well deserved boost, director general Jose Sainz Armada said in an interview on Saturday.
"I think it's going to be a good year for Argentaria's shares," Armada, responsible for wholesale banking and finance, told Spanish financial daily Expansion.
"I hope that the improvement in results during 1997 is reflected in its value and gives investors something to be happy about."
Argentaria, formed in 1991 in a merger of six state-owned banks and savings banks, reported a 58 percent fall in net attributable profit in 1996 to 31.22 billion pesetas.
Armada said competition was becoming intense in the banking sector, but that Argentaria was well placed to deal with it.
"Competition is getting tougher by the day, but I don't see it as a danger for Argentaria in the short term, because we have a solid position," he said.
"In my view, the greatest risk in the long run lies in the effects of a Monetary Union," he added.
With regard to the sale of the remaining 25 percent state stake, Armada said he expected the bank to remain independent.
"I think Argentaria will be an independent and private project for some time to come," he said.
